description: How U.S. electricity changed: coal collapsed while wind and solar surged — a year-by-year race from 2000 to 2026 that reshaped the grid.
youtube_description:
The Grid Flip — A decade-by-decade cinematic race through U.S. electricity generation. Watch how coal — once the undisputed king — collapses under cheap natural gas, aging plants and policy pressures, while wind and solar explode from niche to mainstream. This timeline uses year-by-year net generation (TWh) to show the real reordering of America’s energy mix through real events: the shale gas boom, the 2009 recession, state-level renewable policies, dramatic cost declines in PV and wind, and the post-2015 acceleration in clean energy deployment.

If you like dramatic picture-based charts and chart-race storytelling, subscribe and hit the bell — more timelines like this every week. Share this video if you were surprised by how quickly solar rose.

Sources: U.S. Energy Information Administration historical net generation and short-term outlook (compiled into a visual timeline).

Watch next: “The Car Flip” (how EVs changed transport) — link in the pinned comment.
